newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's July fishmeal output rises 42 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru's July fishmeal output rises 42 percent.

text.p: Peru produced 109,300 tonnes of fishmeal in July, up 42 percent from the same month last year, the government said Wednesday.
A Fisheries' Ministry report also said fishmeal production in the first seven months of the year was 1.153 million tonnes, off 11.6 percent versus the same period last year.

Despite the monthly rise in July's output, exports of fishmeal for the month fell 12.9 percent to 167,500 tonnes, compared with July last year. Exports for the first seven months were down 27.7 percent to 994,800 tonnes, compared with the same period the year before.
The report gave no explanation for the figures.
However, industry officials have blamed fishing bans and sudden temperature changes in the sea for the overall fall in output this year.
Fishmeal, Peru's most important fishing product, accounted for 75 percent of Peru's total processing of 144,800 tonnes of fish and other sea products in July.

Production of Peru's second most important fish product, raw fish oil, was 22,600 tonnes in July, up 71 percent from the same period last year. Output of raw fish oil in the first seven months was 276,900 tonnes, 8.3 percent lower than in the same period last year.
In July, the total catch of Peruvian fish and sea species was up 27.2 percent to 549,700 tonnes compared with the same period last year.
The catch of anchovy, which is used to make fishmeal and fish oil, rose 122 percent in July to 446,600 tonnes, compared with the same month last year.

Peru produced 1.774 million tonnes of fishmeal in 1995, down 24.1 percent from the 2.338 million tonnes processed the previous year. However, the value of fishmeal exports last year rose 4.1 percent to $766.54 million despite an 18.2 percent drop in the volume sold abroad to 1,860,200 tonnes.
Officials said production fell in 1995 due to extended seasonal fishing bans and climatic factors while higher world prices for fishmeal allowed a hike in the value of exports.
